claims.statement: Verified fact: in July 2026 the Commission said EUDR would begin to apply at the end of December 2026 and adopted updated product-scope and Information System measures.
Verified fact: the EUDR Information System supports due-diligence statements, geolocation-file checks, and API-supported features including simplified declarations and grouping.
Hypothesis (unvalidated): midmarket importers will pay for a commercial consignment relay around the free official submission system because upstream exception resolution remains outside it.

contrary_evidence: The Commission's 2026 simplification package updated scope and added official API/grouping features, which may reduce paid workflow pain: https://environment.ec.europa.eu/news/commission-updates-product-scope-and-tools-support-eudr-2026-07-13_en

The official system already validates geolocation-file compatibility and manages legally meaningful statements, so the product cannot rely on form submission as differentiation: https://environment.ec.europa.eu/news/eu-deforestation-regulation-information-system-launches-2024-12-06_en

economics.acquisition_route: Run a fixed-fee evidence-readiness audit through customs or certification partners, then convert one commodity lane to recurring use.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario: 10 importers at PLN 5,000 MRR in year 2, 40 at PLN 7,000 MRR in year 4, and 70 at PLN 8,000 MRR in year 6 imply PLN 6.72m ARR before consignment fees. At a 3-4x ARR value and 60% founder ownership, PLN 5m net worth is plausible in years 5-7; major further scope simplification or failure to obtain upstream data from two lanes invalidates the path.
economics.founder_time: 4-5 hours/day through the first commodity lane; obtain external legal review and avoid acting as the importer of record.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 72-86%; supplier support and geospatial review are variable costs and cannot be hidden inside unlimited plans.
economics.payback: Unvalidated customer hypothesis: avoiding one held consignment or repeated supplier chase can repay several months; validate with shadow processing before application begins.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated estimate: PLN 2,000-9,000 monthly per importer plus PLN 75-350 per released consignment and paid supplier onboarding.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Each inbound consignment repeats the due-diligence linkage; supplier correction histories and ERP mappings are durable.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: supplier-specific correction history and commodity-lane evidence patterns accelerate later consignment clearance while integrations lock in the relay
fingerprint.customer: EU midmarket importers and manufacturers handling EUDR-covered commodities with dozens to hundreds of suppliers rather than global compliance teams
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: customs brokers, commodity testing labs, certification advisers, ERP import modules, and a readiness audit before late-2026 application
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: supplier portal, geofile validation, PO/batch linkage, reference-number relay, exception queue, versioned risk decision, and audit export; subscription plus consignment volume
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: importer pays per active supplier and per released consignment when the evidence token and official reference are complete
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a purchase order or inbound consignment approaches customs or market release without complete geolocation, upstream reference, or risk evidence

founder_fit: Geospatial validation, entity linking, and exception automation use data-science leverage.
A Polish/EU regulatory wedge can be developed without consumer branding or video.
Partner-led audits permit part-time validation before building a network.
Consignment-volume revenue can compound into a data and workflow asset.
risks: EUDR rules and product scope have changed repeatedly and may change again.
Supplier geolocation can be inaccurate, fraudulent, or commercially sensitive.
The product could be mistaken for legal assurance even though responsibility stays with the operator.
Large ERP, traceability, and certification platforms are likely competitors.

structure.control_point: consignment release token linking commercial batch data to due-diligence evidence and official submission reference
structure.critical_dependency: timely, accurate plot geolocation and chain-of-custody data from upstream suppliers plus stable EUDR Information System interfaces

thesis: Create a consignment-level relay for EU importers of coffee, cocoa, wood, rubber, and derived goods: bind supplier geolocation files, product/HS data, upstream due-diligence references, risk decisions, purchase orders, and the EU Information System receipt into one release token before a shipment is placed on the market. The importer remains legally responsible; the tool sells workflow evidence and supplier exception routing, not a blanket compliance guarantee.
title: EUDR Consignment Admissibility Relay for Midmarket Importers
uncertainties: The final late-2026 implementation details and customer urgency are not yet proven.
Importer willingness to force supplier portal adoption is unknown.
The best first commodity lane and minimum evidence depth require interviews.
Official API rate, authorization, and grouping behavior need technical validation.
